user.title: Find your kettle
user.description: Choose your kettle. We check the connection first; afterwards you can choose whether to use Wi-Fi too. If it is missing, search again via Bluetooth. Keep the kettle within range of Home Assistant or a Bluetooth proxy and close the Fellow app.

zeroconf.title: Kettle discovered
zeroconf.description: A Fellow Stagg kettle was found at {base_url}. Add it to Home Assistant?

reconfigure.title: Change kettle URL
reconfigure.description: Enter the kettle's new URL (e.g. after its IP address changed).

wifi_setup.title: Set up Wi-Fi over Bluetooth
wifi_setup.description: Put the kettle in Wi-Fi setup mode from its menu first, and keep the Fellow app closed (it holds the Bluetooth connection, and its own setup also makes the kettle download new firmware). Home Assistant then sends the network details straight to the kettle; nothing goes through Fellow's servers.

data.scan_networks: Scan for networks instead of typing

data_description.ssid: Type the network name — this is the reliable path. 2.4 GHz only; the kettle has no 5 GHz radio.
data_description.password: Leave empty for an open network.
data_description.scan_networks: Leave off and type the name above — that's the reliable way. The kettle reverts its Wi-Fi after a scan, so a scanned session won't stick. Tick this with the name empty to fetch the list anyway.

bluetooth_menu.title: {name}
bluetooth_menu.description: This kettle isn't reachable over Wi-Fi (not set up, or not connected). Set up Wi-Fi over Bluetooth for the full feature set, add it Bluetooth-only for now (you can enable Wi-Fi later), or enter its IP if you know it.

dhcp_confirm.description: Add the Fellow Stagg kettle at {base_url}?

transport_device.title: Connection
transport_device.description: Choose Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or both. Bluetooth-only never connects to the kettle over Wi-Fi. Wi-Fi or Auto also unlocks firmware tools and the screen sensor.

connection_check.title: Check Bluetooth connection
connection_check.description: Close the Fellow app and check Bluetooth range. Submit to try connecting again.

wifi_choice.title: Use Wi-Fi too?
wifi_choice.description:
Bluetooth to {name} has been checked. **Firmware: {firmware}**. Wi-Fi address reported by the kettle: {wifi_address} (reachability not yet checked).

With Wi-Fi, the integration automatically chooses an appropriate connection. Without Wi-Fi, supported firmware allows power, temperature, clock sync, schedules and supported kettle settings over Bluetooth. Firmware tools and the screen sensor are not offered. Available functions depend on firmware.

Skipping Wi-Fi prevents this integration from using or setting up Wi-Fi. It does not switch off existing Wi-Fi on the kettle itself. You can add Wi-Fi later.

data.share_fellow_data: Share data with Fellow (cloud firmware updates & usage metrics)

data_description.share_fellow_data: Off by default. When off, Home Assistant keeps the kettle's firmware-update check disabled. The kettle still sends usage metrics directly to Fellow over your network, and Home Assistant cannot block that traffic — to stop it completely, block qhderznbzup.firmware.fellowproducts.com on your router/DNS or use the kettle over Bluetooth only.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Choose Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or both. Bluetooth-only never connects to the kettle over Wi-Fi. Wi-Fi or Auto also unlocks firmware tools and the screen sensor.

switch_firmware.title: Switch firmware
switch_firmware.description:
The kettle runs **{running_version}** ({running_partition}). This switches it to **{target_version}** ({target_partition}), which is already stored on the kettle, and restarts it. That takes about 10 seconds.

Block the kettle's internet access first, or it may update itself again.

upload_firmware.title: Upload firmware
upload_firmware.description: Select a trusted Fellow Stagg .img or .bin image. Available over the legacy HTTP CLI or native HTTP firmware 1.2.26, with the kettle in standby. BLE-only cannot upload firmware. The integration checks the image header and size; this does not establish authenticity or guarantee recovery. Keep power connected until completion. The kettle restarts; success requires reading back the requested version on the other partition.

factory_reset.title: Restore factory settings
factory_reset.description: This erases the kettle’s saved settings, including Wi-Fi, and restarts it. Firmware and factory calibration are retained. Requires firmware 1.2.26, Bluetooth and standby. Afterwards setup starts again: choose Wi-Fi or Bluetooth only. Home Assistant entities are retained. If you close this dialog, reopen Configure to finish setup.

data.confirm: Yes, erase the kettle settings and start setup again

reset_recovery.title: Check the kettle
reset_recovery.description: The reset or restart could not be confirmed. No reset command will be repeated. Check the kettle and, if needed, complete the factory reset on its menu. Continue to check Bluetooth again and resume setup.

reset_wifi_choice.title: Use Wi-Fi too?
reset_wifi_choice.description: Bluetooth to {name} has been checked. **Firmware: {firmware}**. Choose whether to set up Wi-Fi again. Bluetooth only supports power, temperature, clock sync, schedules and supported kettle settings. Wi-Fi adds firmware tools and the screen sensor. Skipping Wi-Fi keeps this integration Bluetooth-only.

reset_settings.title: Set up the kettle
reset_settings.description:
The factory reset wiped {name}'s settings. Restore a starter set now, pre-filled from Home Assistant — you can change any of these later from the kettle's entities. Target temperature is in °C.

Firmware auto-update can't be set over Bluetooth: it's a signed cloud setting. To keep your firmware, turn Auto-update off in the kettle's own menu, and (on Wi-Fi) enable the Lock firmware switch. The Brew guide is set too, but the kettle can't confirm it over Bluetooth, so it's applied best-effort.

abort.no_other_firmware: The kettle is running {running_version} and its other partition holds no valid firmware to switch to. Use Upload firmware (recovery) to put a different version there first.
abort.firmware_same_version: Both partitions are running {running_version}, so there is nothing to upgrade or downgrade to. Use Upload firmware (recovery) to flash a different version first; then you can switch back and forth.
abort.firmware_switch_failed: The kettle didn't come back on {target_version} within a minute. Check the **Firmware version** sensor in a moment; if the switch didn't take, the kettle keeps its previous firmware.
abort.firmware_uploaded: Done: the kettle restarted on firmware {version}.
abort.firmware_upload_failed: The kettle didn't come back after the firmware {version} upload within the time limit. Check the Firmware version sensor; if it didn't take, the kettle keeps its previous firmware.
abort.not_loaded: The kettle isn't loaded yet; try again in a moment.
abort.ble_unreachable: Could not connect to the kettle over Bluetooth. Is it in range of Home Assistant's Bluetooth adapter or a Bluetooth proxy, and is the Fellow app closed?
abort.wifi_setup_done: The kettle is now on {ssid} at {ip}.
abort.legacy_firmware_required: Switching partitions needs the kettle’s legacy Wi-Fi HTTP interface (setpart/reset). It is on {running_version} over {transport} now, so switching is not available. It works on firmware whose local CLI responds, e.g. after a rollback.
abort.firmware_upload_unavailable: Uploading firmware needs the kettle's Wi-Fi HTTP connection, but it is on {transport} now. Set the connection mode to Auto (Configure → Connection) and enter the kettle's URL, then try again. Bluetooth-only cannot upload firmware.
abort.firmware_not_read: Home Assistant can't read the kettle's firmware partitions over {transport}. Switching and uploading firmware need the kettle's Wi-Fi HTTP connection — set the connection mode to Auto (Configure → Connection) and enter the kettle's URL, then try again.
abort.firmware_http_unreachable: A kettle URL is set ({url}), but Home Assistant can't reach the kettle over HTTP there, so firmware switching and upload aren't available. Check the kettle is powered on and reachable at that address from Home Assistant's network (not just over Bluetooth), then try again.
abort.reset_requires_ble: Factory reset requires Bluetooth or Auto mode and a saved Bluetooth address. Wi-Fi-only mode is kept exclusive.
abort.reset_unavailable: No reset command was sent — the kettle couldn't be reached over Bluetooth in time. Make sure it's in range of Home Assistant's Bluetooth adapter or a proxy, firmware 1.2.26 is installed, and the Fellow app is closed, then try again. The kettle no longer needs to be on standby first.
abort.reset_setup_done: Setup completed. The kettle uses Bluetooth only.

set_schedule.name: Set schedule
set_schedule.description: Set scheduled time/temperature and optionally enable the schedule.

disable_schedule.name: Disable schedule
disable_schedule.description: Disable scheduled start on the kettle.

update_schedule.name: Update schedule
update_schedule.description: Apply the current schedule time/temp/mode from entities to the kettle.

heat_to.name: Heat to temperature
heat_to.description: Set the target temperature and start heating in one call.

play_chime.name: Play chime
play_chime.description: Play a chime on the kettle's buzzer.

send_cli.name: Send CLI command
send_cli.description: Read-only diagnostic CLI command: state, fwinfo, prtsettings or pwmprt.

install_firmware.name: Install firmware (temporarily disabled)
install_firmware.description: Temporarily disabled on all transports pending safety and recovery validation. Retained for compatibility; no file is read and no kettle command is sent.

path.name: Firmware file path
path.description: Absolute path to the .img file, readable by Home Assistant (e.g. under /config, /media or /share).

entry_id.description: Optional config entry id (needed if multiple kettles)
entry_id.name: Kettle (config entry)

get_settings_snapshot.name: Read settings snapshot
get_settings_snapshot.description: Read native/BLE settings for supervised testing. No setting or power command is sent. Contains clock/settings values, no network identifiers.

start_ble_trace.name: Start live BLE recording
start_ble_trace.description: Read-only B1/B5 recording, memory only, maximum 120 seconds.

get_ble_trace.name: Read live BLE recording
get_ble_trace.description: Read timestamped frames; stops recording by default.

probe_schedule_console.name: Probe schedule console
probe_schedule_console.description: Experimental: send one read-only prtsettings query and listen on B6 for eight seconds. Returns only recognized schedule fields and capture counts. Requires current standby state; no schedule or power setting is changed.

set_existing_schedule_mode.name: Change existing schedule mode
set_existing_schedule_mode.description: Change a physically configured future schedule to once/daily, or disable it. Firmware 1.2.26 with Bluetooth or Wi-Fi required. Once/daily cannot be read back: check the physical menu. Does not change time or temperature.

restore_standby_display.name: Restore standby display (Wi-Fi)
restore_standby_display.description: Temporarily turn the standby clock off and restore its original digital/analog mode. Requires firmware 1.2.26, Wi-Fi, standby and planning off. Check the visual result.

cli_muted.title: No valid CLI data
cli_muted.description: Firmware {version} does not return valid CLI data. Native HTTP is detected from valid responses; BLE is available for 1.2.26. This integration does not switch firmware automatically. The other partition reports {other_version}.

firmware_staged.title: Firmware {staged} is stored on the kettle
firmware_staged.description: The kettle runs {running}; partition {partition} contains {staged}, which may start after a restart. Turn on the **Lock firmware** switch to have Home Assistant switch the kettle back to its pinned firmware (over the legacy HTTP CLI) whenever it updates itself. A router rule that blocks the kettle's internet while keeping local Wi-Fi is more reliable if you can set one.

wifi_offline.title: Wi-Fi offline — kettle running on Bluetooth

setup_wifi.title: Reconnect Wi-Fi
setup_wifi.description: The kettle is running on Bluetooth because its Wi-Fi isn't reachable. Put the kettle in Wi-Fi setup mode from its menu and keep the Fellow app closed, then enter a network below. Home Assistant sends it to the kettle over Bluetooth; nothing goes through Fellow's servers. 2.4 GHz only.

error.ble_unreachable: Couldn't reach the kettle over Bluetooth. Make sure it's awake, nearby, and in Wi-Fi setup mode, then try again.
error.provision_failed: Setting up Wi-Fi failed. Check the network name and password (2.4 GHz only) and try again.
